name: Taiwan Employment Gold Card

faqs.question: What is the 4-in-1 mechanism of the Gold Card?
faqs.answer: The Employment Gold Card combines four permits into a single physical card: (1) Open Work Permit — work for any employer without sponsorship, (2) Resident Visa — legal entry into Taiwan, (3) Alien Resident Certificate (ARC) — proof of legal residency, and (4) Re-entry Permit — leave and re-enter Taiwan freely. This eliminates the need for separate applications to multiple agencies.

faqs.question: Do I need an employer to sponsor my Gold Card application?
faqs.answer: No. The Gold Card is entirely self-sponsored. You apply directly through the Foreign Professionals Online Application Platform. No employer, company, or institution needs to sponsor or submit paperwork on your behalf. This is one of the key differences from a standard Work ARC.

faqs.question: What are the industry fields for Gold Card qualification?
faqs.answer: The 12 designated professional fields are: (1) Science & Technology, (2) Digital, (3) Finance, (4) Education, (5) Architecture, (6) Culture and Arts, (7) Sports, (8) Biotechnology, (9) Economy, (10) National Defense, (11) Law, (12) Environmental Protection. Additionally, 'Practitioners of Ancestor Rites' (宗教專業人士) is recognized as a specialized qualification path. Each field has its own set of sub-tracks with specific qualification criteria. The government periodically expands the list — check the official Gold Card portal for the latest fields.

faqs.question: How does the salary track work (NT$160,000/month)?
faqs.answer: The salary track is available across most professional fields. Applicants must demonstrate a monthly salary of at least NT$160,000 (~USD $5,000) using tax returns or employer salary certificates. You may choose any 1 year within the past 3 years for evidence — pick the year with the highest documented income. Acceptable documents include W-2 (US), P60 (UK), T4 (Canada), PAYG (Australia), or PIT-11 (Poland).

faqs.question: Can I switch professional fields after receiving the Gold Card?
faqs.answer: The Gold Card is tied to the professional field approved during the application. You cannot change the field on an active Gold Card. However, when applying for renewal, you may specify a different professional field, provided you meet that field's qualification criteria with supporting documentation.

faqs.question: How does the 50% tax exemption work?
faqs.answer: Gold Card holders who meet all of the following conditions receive a 50% income tax exemption on annual salary exceeding NT$3,000,000 for their first 5 years: (1) first-time employment in Taiwan (no prior Taiwan employment history), (2) physically present in Taiwan for 183+ days per calendar year, and (3) no Taiwan household registration in the prior 5 years. The exemption applies only to the portion of salary above NT$3M — income below that threshold is taxed at normal rates.

faqs.question: Can my family join me in Taiwan with the Gold Card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Spouses and minor children may apply for Dependent ARC status, which provides legal residency in Taiwan. Parents and grandparents may apply for multiple-entry Visitor Visas valid for up to 1 year. As of 2026, spouses of Gold Card holders can also apply for open work permits, allowing them to work for any employer in Taiwan without separate sponsorship.

faqs.question: How long does the APRC fast-track take for Gold Card holders?
faqs.answer: Gold Card holders are eligible for an Alien Permanent Resident Certificate (APRC) after 3 years of continuous residency, compared to 5 years for regular foreign residents. High-income earners (annual salary NT$6,000,000 or above) may apply after only 1 year. Holders of a PhD from a Taiwan institution receive an additional 2-year reduction. Holders of a Master's degree from a Taiwan institution receive a 1-year reduction.

faqs.question: What happens if my Gold Card application is rejected?
faqs.answer: The application fee is non-refundable regardless of the outcome. You may re-apply after addressing the reasons for rejection. Common rejection reasons include: currently holding an ineligible visa status (Working Holiday, blue-collar work visa, APEC card, language study visa), insufficient or unverifiable documentation, missing official seals on employment certificates, and failure to provide supplementary documents within the required deadline.

faqs.question: Can I renew my Gold Card?
faqs.answer: Yes. Apply for renewal within 4 months before the expiration date via the same online application platform. You must still meet the original eligibility criteria for your professional field at the time of renewal. Renewal processing typically takes 2-4 weeks and costs NT$1,500-3,500 depending on the duration chosen.

faqs.question: What documents are strictly required for employment certificates?
faqs.answer: Employment certificates submitted for the Gold Card must include all of the following: (1) your full legal name, (2) company name, (3) your position title, (4) actual employment period (start and end dates), and (5) an official company seal or authorized signature. Offer letters, generic reference letters, and certificates without seals are NOT accepted and will result in a request for supplementary documents or rejection.

faqs.question: Can I convert from a Working Holiday or language study visa to a Gold Card?
faqs.answer: No. Holders of Working Holiday visas, APEC Business Travel Cards, blue-collar work visas, and Chinese language study visas cannot convert to a Gold Card while in Taiwan. You must exit Taiwan and re-apply from overseas through the online platform. This restriction applies regardless of whether you meet the professional field qualification criteria.

pathsTo.name: Alien Permanent Resident Certificate
pathsTo.requirements: Gold Card holders: 3 years continuous residency (vs 5 years for normal foreigners). High earners (NT$6M+/year): only 1 year. Taiwan PhD: additional 2-year reduction. Taiwan Master's: 1-year reduction.
pathsTo.notes: The most common long-term path for Gold Card holders. APRC provides permanent residency without renewal requirements.

pathsTo.name: Job-Seeking ARC
pathsTo.requirements: Gold Card holders who are unable to find work may apply for a 6+6 month job-seeking ARC within 3 months before Gold Card expiry.
pathsTo.timeline: Apply within 3 months of Gold Card expiry, 2-4 weeks processing
pathsTo.notes: A bridge option for Gold Card holders who cannot renew but want to remain in Taiwan to seek employment.

pathsFrom.name: Digital Nomad Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: DNV holders who meet Gold Card qualification criteria in any of the 12 professional fields may apply while on active DNV status in Taiwan.
pathsFrom.notes: Common upgrade path for digital nomads who want Taiwan work permission, NHI access, and tax benefits. Can apply domestically while on DNV.

pathsFrom.name: Work ARC (Employment-Sponsored)
pathsFrom.requirements: Existing Work ARC holders may apply for Gold Card upgrade if they meet qualification criteria. Previous ARC will be cancelled upon Gold Card issuance.
pathsFrom.notes: For ARC holders seeking open work permission and tax benefits. Gold Card removes employer tie.

pathsFrom.name: Visa-Exempt Entry / Visitor Visa
pathsFrom.requirements: Applicants in Taiwan on visa-exempt entry or visitor visa may apply domestically. Most common entry path for first-time applicants.
pathsFrom.notes: The most common pathway. Enter Taiwan visa-exempt, apply online while in-country. Ensure you select the correct application category for your current status.
